To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
sub-2 nm graphene pores display diverse ion transport behaviours that can be understood in terms of ion dehydration and electrokinetics.

graphene nanopores exhibit diverse, sub-continuum, heterogeneous ionic transport consistent with a free-energy barrier for ion transport, and that a modified Nernst–Planck model incorporating ionic dehydration and electric field effects quantitatively describes the observed behaviour.
isolated sub-continuum transport through graphene nanopores displays heterogeneous behaviours that are consistent with ion transport in the vicinity of a free-energy barrier.

the observed behaviours in graphene nanopores below 1 nm are a direct result of the interplay between the ion dehydration, electrostatic interactions, and electrokinetic phenomena.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have demonstrated that graphene nanopores exhibit heterogeneous transport behaviour and that the transport characteristics of graphene nanopores are determined by the pore size, the pore environment, and the ion type.

the transport properties of graphene nanopores are diverse and depend on the pore structure, and that a modified Nernst–Planck model can be used to quantitatively explain the observed transport behaviours.

the ionic transport behaviour in isolated graphene nanopores is diverse, and that this behaviour can be understood by a model that accounts for the effects of dehydration and electrostatic forces on ion transport.
The main takeaway from our work is that
sub-continuum ion transport in graphene nanopores is highly diverse and that this diversity can be exploited for applications such as ion sensing.

the transport properties of sub-2 nanometre pores in graphene membranes can vary widely, and this diversity can be exploited to create a new class of nanoporous membranes for ionic separation and sensing applications.
the transport properties of graphene nanopores can be tuned by controlling the pore diameter and the pore environment, thus opening a route towards nanopore-based ion separation and sensing.
